claim_verdicts.evidence: Longhorn 1.9.0 Concepts (WebFetch): Longhorn is "a resilient distributed block storage system"; snapshots/replicas "are stored on the disk of the nodes within the Kubernetes cluster"; the engine "synchronously replicates the volume across the multiple replicas stored on multiple nodes"; "The Longhorn CSI driver takes the block device, formats it, and mounts it on the node." Storage Class Parameters: provisioner, "For Longhorn, that is always 'driver.longhorn.io'."

Storage Class Parameters 1.9.0: numberOfReplicas "The desired number of copies (replicas) for redundancy", default 3. Settings 1.9.0: Replica Node Level Soft Anti-Affinity, default false: "When this setting is checked, the Longhorn Manager will allow scheduling on nodes with existing healthy replicas" of the same volume - so unchecked (default) places each replica on a different node. Concepts: "Each replica should be placed on a different node or on different disks."

Concepts 1.9.0: "The Longhorn Engine always runs in the same node as the Pod that uses the Longhorn volume." "It synchronously replicates the volume across the multiple replicas stored on multiple nodes." Settings 1.9.0: V1 Data Engine default true; Engine Replica Timeout (v1) = how long the engine waits for a replica response before marking it failed - supports the round-2 addition that a replica that stops answering is marked failed and no longer waited for.

Round 2: text now matches round-1 suggested_text (no ranking). Concepts 1.9.0: the engine "synchronously replicates the volume across the multiple replicas stored on multiple nodes"; Best Practices 1.9.0: "Foreground IOs to the replicas" are latency-sensitive. A synchronous wait on remote replicas adds to each write's completion time.

local-path-provisioner README: "will create either hostPath or local based persistent volume on the node automatically." "By default, PersistentVolumes created by the provisioner use the kubernetes.io/hostname label for node affinity." "This ensures the volume is only accessible on the node where it was provisioned."

Round 2: text now carries the condition. Node Failure Handling 1.9.0: replacement pod "will get stuck in ContainerCreating state"; StatefulSet pods are not force-deleted by Kubernetes; "After force deleting, Kubernetes will detach the Longhorn volume and spin up replacement pods on a new node." Settings 1.9.0: Pod Deletion Policy When Node is Down, default do-nothing.

Concepts 1.9.0: "If the current healthy replica count is less than specified replica count, Longhorn will start rebuilding new replicas"; rebuild syncs data "from a good replica to the blank replica." Settings 1.9.0: Replica Node Level Soft Anti-Affinity default false (scheduling on a node with an existing healthy replica of the volume is not allowed). Hence on 3 nodes / 3 replicas / 1 node down there is no eligible node. Note: Replica Replenishment Wait Interval (default 600 s) delays the rebuild; lesson's "then" is not contradicted.

Round-2 text ('the lab does not set this up'). Installation Requirements 1.9.0: "open-iscsi is installed, and the iscsid daemon is running on all the nodes." Grep (?i)iscsi over examples/don-hang: only hit is longhorn-storageclass.yaml L2 (a comment); no kind config, script or manifest installs open-iscsi. The repo comment's stronger 'kind's nodes lack' stays unverified (Docker engine still not running on review host) - see issue.

refs storage-classes.md L177-180: "The `Immediate` mode indicates that volume binding and dynamic provisioning occurs once the PersistentVolumeClaim is created", "without knowledge of the Pod's scheduling requirements". L139-144: expansion "allows you to resize the volume by editing the corresponding PVC" when "`allowVolumeExpansion` set to true". persistent-volumes.md L203-207: Delete removes the PV and "the associated storage asset". Longhorn SC params 1.9.0: provisioner "always driver.longhorn.io".

tools/extract-code --tag stage-3: base/db.yaml volumeClaimTemplates `data` with no storageClassName (comment: "With no storageClassName it gets the cluster's default StorageClass"), replicas: 1; base/rabbitmq.yaml same shape, one node, replicas: 1. No manifest at stage-3 quoted in the lesson references longhorn-replicated outside deploy/k8s/bare-metal/, whose header says "Read, not installed".

Concepts 1.9.0: the engine "synchronously replicates the volume across the multiple replicas" (every replica receives the same writes); "Snapshots are stored locally, as a part of each replica of a volume." "A backup is an object in the backupstore, which is an NFS or S3 compatible object store external to the Kubernetes cluster." Deleting the volume: see claim 9.

Labelled opinion; round 2 states it with its condition in section 6 ("under a database whose team already fails over to a standby") and hedged in section 5 ("would mostly add slower writes"). Factual parts covered by claims 3, 4.

issues.text: Carried from round 1. Repo comment outside the quoted range (longhorn-storageclass.yaml L18-19 at stage-3, unchanged) contradicts Longhorn 1.9 docs: staleReplicaTimeout is "Minutes after a replica is marked unhealthy before it is deemed useless for rebuilds and is just deleted", not the wait before rebuilding elsewhere. Lesson text unaffected.
issues.quote: # Minutes a failed replica is kept before Longhorn gives up on it and
issues.fix: Propose via prompt 08 (already in meta repo_changes_needed): "Minutes after a replica is marked unhealthy before Longhorn stops using it for rebuilds and deletes it." No change to this lesson.

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed paragraph). The Pod is called "stuck", but the lesson does not say what it is stuck in or why the StatefulSet does not replace it by itself. I can accept the rule, but I could not explain it to someone else.
issues.quote: Kubernetes does not replace a StatefulSet Pod on a failed node by itself: someone deletes the stuck Pod (Longhorn has a setting to do it, off by default).
issues.fix: Add one clause after 'by itself' saying what state the old Pod is left in and why that stops the StatefulSet from starting a replacement until it is deleted.
